speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis. The clinical presentation of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old infant, often referred to as "cradle cap," combined with a family history of psoriasis (an inflammatory skin condition), is characteristic of this diagnosis. The worsening in cold weather and the "erythematous patches" description fit the typical inflammatory course. While a biopsy was requested earlier, the clinical picture is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, which is a common, benign condition in infants that often improves with age. No further tests are required at this time as the diagnosis is clinically secure.
